llm.label: LLM
llm.desc: The AI model an Agent thinks with. Several Agents can share one.

agent.label: Agent
agent.desc: The AI worker you hand a job to. You give it a role, a goal and a backstory.

task.label: Task
task.desc: One job for an Agent. You say what to do and what you want back.

tool.label: Tool
tool.desc: Something you hand an Agent, like web search — things the model can't do alone.

crew.label: Crew
crew.desc: Bundles your Agents and Tasks into one team and runs them. Exactly one per canvas.

input.label: Input
input.desc: A value you fill in each run. Drop it into a Task description as {name}.

output.label: Output
output.desc: Where the final result shows up when the run finishes.

knowledge.label: Knowledge
knowledge.desc: Reference material for an Agent. It looks up the relevant parts as it works.

memory.label: Memory
memory.desc: Lets the Crew remember what came earlier. Leave it unwired and the Crew's own setting applies.

human.label: Human Input
human.desc: Shows you the result before it moves on. Approve it, or send notes and have it redone.

router.label: Router
router.desc: Splits the flow down different paths depending on a condition. (planned for v1.1)

guardrail.label: Guardrail
guardrail.desc: Sends the work back to be redone if the result misses the mark. (planned for v1.1)

note.label: Note
note.desc: A note you leave on the canvas. It has no effect on the run.

group.label: Group
group.desc: Wraps several nodes in one frame so they move together.

nodeBody.outputWaiting: The result appears here once the run finishes.

tutorial.stepsHeading: Seven steps to your first run
tutorial.step1Desc: Grab a key from whichever provider you want to use (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Groq) and drop it into API Keys in the header. Keys stay in this browser — they never end up in canvas files or share links. Running Ollama on your own machine instead? You need no key at all: go straight to step 2.
tutorial.step2Desc: A template gets you moving much faster than a blank canvas. Open Templates in the header, pick whichever is closest to what you want, and hit Use this. Every card tells you which keys it needs and roughly what one run costs. First time? Hello Crew is the simplest, and the local summarizer needs no key at all.
tutorial.step3Title: Add nodes and wire them up
tutorial.step3Desc: Drag nodes in from the list on the left, or right-click the canvas, then drag between the dots (sockets) to connect them. The usual order is: what it uses (LLM, Tool, Knowledge) → Agent → Task → Crew → Output. Pairs that don't belong together simply refuse to connect, so feel free to experiment. Ctrl+K finds and adds anything instantly.
tutorial.step4Desc: Click any node and its fields open on the right. Tell the LLM which provider and model to use, give the Agent a role, a goal and a backstory, and tell the Task what to do and what you want back. The model list only offers what your registered keys can actually reach right now.
tutorial.step5Desc: Anything you left blank or wired up wrong gets a red badge on the node, with the reason and a code (AC-Exxx) in the panel on the right. Click the error count in the header and it walks you through the problem nodes one at a time. The run button stays locked until every one is gone, so clear them here.
tutorial.step6Title: Try it first with Dry Run
tutorial.step6Desc: Dry Run walks through everything without calling the AI, so it costs nothing. It shows you the order things will happen in and what a real run would cost — worth a click before you spend anything.
tutorial.step7Title: Run it and keep the result
tutorial.step7Desc: Hit Queue Prompt and it runs for real. You can watch how far it's got on the nodes and in the log below, and results land in the Output node. Happy with it? Save it to your own templates, or use Export Code to download a Python script that runs without AgentCanvas.
tutorial.stepsFootnote: Your work saves to this browser on every edit, so there's nothing to remember to save. To move it to another machine or keep a backup, use Backup / Restore to export it to a file and load it back.
tutorial.title: Tutorial — Getting Started
tutorial.intro: New here? These seven steps take you all the way to your first run. Below them you'll find what each of the 14 node types does, and the order they stack in when a crew runs.
tutorial.diagramAria: The order nodes stack in — step 1 what it uses (LLM, Tool, Knowledge, Memory, Input), step 2 the Agent who does it, step 3 the Task, step 4 the Crew, step 5 the result
tutorial.layer1Desc: Everything an Agent draws on. Input is dashed because it takes no wire — it fills the {variable} slots in a Task description at run time.
tutorial.layer2Desc: Give it a role, a goal and a backstory and it puts all of that to work.
tutorial.layer3Desc: One job handed to an Agent. Chain them with next / depends on and that becomes the order.
tutorial.layer4Desc: Bundles the Agents and Tasks into one team and runs them. Exactly one per canvas.
tutorial.layer5Desc: The finished result lands here once the run is done.
tutorial.utilsDesc: Keeps things readable. No effect on the run.

human.closeHint: Respond, or cancel the run with Stop in the header — the backend is blocked waiting.

human.feedbackPlaceholder: Leave it empty and press 'Approve and continue' to proceed as-is. Write something and press 'Send revision request' and the agent reruns with your feedback, then asks again.

runparams.title: Run parameters
runparams.intro: Fill in the values declared by the Input nodes on the canvas. Values from your last run are pre-filled.
runparams.introDryRun: A Dry Run only shows the execution order and estimated cost — no real LLM calls.
